snippet.title: Doctor Strange Multiverse Of Madness Scenes That Were Completely CGI
snippet.description:
It seems like Marvel ups the game every time for CGI effects - and with Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness - they may have just toppled all the competition. It’s normal for most productions to shoot as practical as possible for time sake and believability - but this MCU film went above and beyond to nail down the madness in this adventure of Doctor Strange.
Traveling through multiple universes - means a whole lot of the MCU special effects needed to be as realistic as possible. The team used the real actors in harnesses and surrounded them in bright green backgrounds - to effectively immerse them into the digital worlds. That’s a whole lot of imagination from Benedict Cumberbatch - since he fights everything from one-eyed monsters to demons. The great thing about Marvel - is that they give us great looks at how they pull off these effects behind the scenes. How do they even coordinate the effects and actor actions so seamlessly? Topping that with a film as massive in production quality as this one - means for a pretty tough time in making the sequences as believable as possible.
Marvel CGI has gotten so clean in just the past decade - that we would have never been able to tell at times whether or not CGI was used in a scene. Paired with the right director and of course - Oscar nominated actors - a movie with this much CGI can succeed in fooling a few audience members. We’re not saying we thought they actually obtained a one-eyed monster or anything - but the amount of times they didn’t use practical sets and effects - really shocked us.

snippet.title: 15 Vecna Designs That Didn't Make The Cut For Stranger Things
snippet.description:
We can’t stop talking about how terrifying Jamie Campbell Bower is as Vecna in Stranger Things season four. The Duffer Brothers love having a ton of practical effects on set – Vecna was no different. Jamie spent over eight hours a day getting into his Vecna design prosthetics, but did you know there were actually a ton of other designs we could have ended up with? The incredible concept artist, Michael Maher Jr. went all out when designing Stranger Things’ newest big bad. There were designs that were inspired by a prehistoric fish, Alien, Predator, a sort of, Creepypasta smiling character, and tons of other, fleshy, gory depictions. A big influence behind these designs was Henry’s time spent in the Upside Down. Michael Maher Jr. wondered what kind of effect being in a place like that for so long would have on the human body. You’ll see what we mean when we pull up a few of these designs. A big reason a lot of these designs were scrapped, was because it limited Jamie’s ability to utilize his facial expressions to give us that deep, personal scare factor we’re all seeing in our Vecna-induced nightmares. In the end, they seemed to stick with the Hellraiser and Nightmare on Elm Street, humanoid version of Vecna we all hate to love. Stick around and let us know if you think any of the scrapped designs were scarier than the one we ended up with.

snippet.title: Bullet Train Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Bullet Train is one of the most fun and action-packed blockbusters there is - this team didn’t hold back on anything! 
To say there were a lot of intense stunts is putting it lightly. Aaron Taylor-Johnson wound up suffering a really serious injury, while Joey King brought the heat doing her own fights. Brad Pitt does an impressive 90 percent of his stunts, showing off why he’s one of the most famous movie stars in the world. The stunts were extra special, and a lot of attention was paid to them in part because the director, David Leitch started off his career as a stunt man. He wasn’t just anyone’s stunt man though. He doubled for Brad Pitt on some of his most famous movies! 
Most of the film takes place inside a bullet train - so it’s pretty shocking that there wasn’t a single real bullet train to be seen on set! Instead, the team brought impressive sets to life that brought their world to life. This was helped by the fact that there were giant screens that played the rushing scenery we’d see in from inside the train. Oh, and there weren’t actually as many train cars as we saw - they were just very cleverly built and made building the world easy.
Joey King may surprise you in the movie with the accent she does, and if you don’t already know who she is, you definitely won’t now! She spent a load of time training with a dialect coach while Brad Pitt worked with trainers and the stunt team to get into tip-top shape for the movie. 
It was an intense journey to get the film out, but so worth it in the end when you get a film like Bullet Train!

snippet.title: The Gray Man Behind the Scenes

The Gray Man is pushing to become the next big action movie franchise so the Russo Brothers and the rest of the stacked cast put their heart and soul into making sure it gets there. Two hundred million dollars goes a long way. Being the most money Netflix has ever invested in a film. With Ryan Gosling leading the helm in his first ever action movie, he blew the Russo's away with his dance choreography training that came in handy for the fight scenes and even made him a more impressive stage combat fighter than Captain America's Chris Evans himself! Most action movies get about four stunt scenes but this one was paired down from the novel's eleven to nine. Nine! That's actually insane. About three quarters of the movie is all action sequences. One hilarious moment was compared to Monty Python she. Director Joe Russo showed Ryan Gosling how a stunt is done by stepping in himself. Did you know this movie had almost no cut scenes? Post-production can't be understated. But the only scene that did have cuts was that hospital scene because they were experimenting with a ton of different stuff. Despite the movie being called The Gray Man, it's chocked full of colour. This was done intentionally to capture the audience's attention but they did use subtle lighting and filmmaking techniques to help the gray man fade into the background just a little bit. snippet.title: The Voices Behind Minions: The Rise of Gru

The Minions are back - and so are loads of our favorite actors from the franchise! Minions: The Rise of Gru features a whole lot of our favorite voices and some new ones that got us really excited - and some of them might not be who you think they are!
Steve Carell is back as Gru, the only difference this time is that he had to pitch up quite a bit to make himself sound like little Gru! Then, of course, there’s the actor that is one of the driving factors behind the Despicable Me franchise in its entirety - since he not only voices the most characters but happens to lend his hand to writing, producing, and directing as well. A legend of the screen, who happens to have had multiple incredible films come out in 2022, lends their voice to a very fun character - any guesses which other animated feature they did around the same time?? There is some real-life royalty included in this cast - we’re talking about a real-life Dame whose voice many of us have come to know as that of “Lady Whistledown”. 
Some characters were voiced by action stars of the screen - and one of their names definitely gives away which cast member they wound up playing! One actor behind a cameo character happens to be multi-talented, so honestly, we’re a bit surprised they didn’t end up rapping at some point in the movie!
No matter how long the actor had been part of the franchise, every single performer brought their characters to life in the best way.
